J Anxiety Disord 45:49-59, doi:10.1016/j.janxdis.2016.11.008 (author manuscript https://pure.ulster.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/76956283/PTSD_Network_Manuscript_Full_final_version.docx); OSF mj5wa (CC BY 4.0): PTSD_data.sav (https://osf.io/download/vuf6m/, no labels on Q28_01_MONTH..Q28_20_MONTH) and the authors' PTSD_code.R (https://osf.io/download/a9kvc/); processing script data/armour_2017_pcl5.py; wording: PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5), Weathers FW, Litz BT, Keane TM, Palmieri PA, Marx BP, Schnurr PP (2013), NCPTSD standard form https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/documents/PCL5_Standard_form.PDF (version date 29 August 2023, sha256 80e133dd9eb977bef1aa21401ec8c8b19fecaec7856437bc2dcc3a44b5c07bd3, fetched 2026-09-29); rights page https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/adult-sr/ptsd-checklist.asp (fetched 2026-09-29, sha256 766ce2721d6b862725ff507f8db98fbe83fe0f51920c52c050fa549f3ee4a428; the register's 9ada2641 prefix is an earlier fetch of the same page, clause text unchanged)
note: item_text, instructions and the five anchors are the NCPTSD PCL-5 standard form, transcribed verbatim (20/20 item strings found verbatim in the form's extracted text; leading item numbers stripped; curly quotes around 'superalert' kept). The deposit carries no item wording: PTSD_data.sav has no variable or value labels on Q28_01_MONTH..Q28_20_MONTH, and neither the author manuscript nor PTSD_Supplementary.pdf reproduces items -- so text_source=canonical_instrument. The study was a Sept-Oct 2013 GfK KnowledgePanel web survey; its own screen wording is unpublished, and the form shipped is the current (2023-dated) version, whose instruction reads 'select one of the numbers'. The paper states the PCL-5 was administered for past-month symptoms 'in relation to this worst event' (the THS worst event) with anchors '0=Not at all; 1=A little bit; 2=Moderately; 3=Quite a bit; 4=Extremely', matching the shipped 'Keeping your worst event in mind' paragraph and anchors. Code derivation: data/armour_2017_pcl5.py renames Q28_{i:02d}_MONTH -> pcl5_{i} (number-preserving); live pcl5_n equals deposit Q28_nn exactly for all 20 columns (221 values each, unique match). Q28_nn -> PCL-5 item n is tied by the authors' PTSD_code.R, which names the 20 columns in file order B1..E6 ('IntT','NgtM','FshB',...,'DfCon','sDis'), and the paper reports its results in those labels; hence mapping_basis=paper_explicit (study materials, not data labels). Verified PARTIAL against the paper's reported network results and content markers -- see verification_armour_2017_pcl5.csv. Rights: applied instrument_rights_register.csv verdict ship_with_note for the PCL-5 (not re-derived; no register row written). The NCPTSD page, re-read 2026-09-29: "This measure was developed by staff at VA's National Center for PTSD and is in the public domain and not copyrighted. In accordance with the American Psychological Association's ethical guidelines, this instrument is intended for use by qualified health professionals and researchers." The second sentence names an intended user and reserves no right (no fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution term) -- a fitness disclaimer, LOT-R shape, so it does not block. The paper itself is CC BY-NC-ND, but no wording was copied from it.
public_note: The item wording is the published PCL-5 standard form from the National Center for PTSD, not the study's own survey screens, which were not published; the paper confirms past-month ratings about the respondent's worst event on the same five 0-4 anchors

note: Item codes are the deposit's own column names V501-V520; the questionnaire numbers the benefit items 1-20 and each V5nn is taken as item nn (paper_explicit). The deposit Code sheet labels only 14 of 20 codes and its V503 label ('Treatment of spasticity in multiple sclerosis') is questionnaire item 16's content, not item 3's ('Improve spasticity'); RDS-II estimates (weight 1/network size) reproduce all 14 Table 3 percentages to 0.1 and place 'spasticity in MS' 73.8 on V516 (V503 = 79.6), so the Code-sheet V503 label is a codebook error and questionnaire numbering was used for all 20 items. Thai wording: the s001 PDF text layer maps several THSarabunPSK tone-mark/vowel glyphs to ASCII (e.g. J, P, 5, b, 1, E, backslash); corrected to the proper Thai combining characters and checked against page renders at 200 dpi and by automated remapping of the text layer (20/20 identical). Thai items are full sentences each opening with 'กัญชา' (cannabis) under the table heading 'การรับรู้ต่อประโยชน์และโทษของการใช้กัญชา'; the study's English renders the heading as 'Perception of benefit and harm: Cannabis can…' with terse stems, shipped verbatim as the translation (including the source typo 'spasticity form multiple sclerosis' in item 16). The study's English is not word-for-word: item 14 'Reduce nausea and vomiting' omits the Thai 'จากเคมีบำบัด' (from chemotherapy); item 5 omits 'and reduce weight loss'; item 7 renders the Thai 'stress disorder after facing disaster' as PTSD. Options ใช่/ไม่ใช่ (Yes/No) from the questionnaire column heads; Code sheet 1=Yes 2=No, script recodes 1->1, 2->0; the Table 3 reproduction uses resp=1 as 'yes' (insomnia 99.1), confirming direction. Administered by face-to-face interview (per processing script). Rights: study-authored checklist, no external instrument; silence, published CC BY 4.0.
